v.why: Replacing an identity with pooling blurs features and usually hurts, while pooling over none at least adds a path.
Pool replacing skip loses the identity signal, unlike pool replacing none.
Pooling over none adds a parameter-free path to the output, whereas pooling over skip degrades one.
The 1x1 to 3x3 upgrade is a smaller step than adding a new conv path, and the 1x1 already supplies learnable features.
Kernel enlargement over a 1x1 conv is a modest gain relative to adding a conv path, particularly at low resolution.
A conv on edge 4 makes node 1 a strong route to the output, so improving its input pays off.
When edge 1 is the only input to node 2, its quality directly determines what edge 5 passes on.
Edge 4 already supplies strong conv features to node 3, so edge 5's upgrade is less valuable.
Another conv summed at node 3 gives redundant features, so the gain from edge 3 shrinks.
Edge 4 as skip provides an identity-like route to the output when no direct edge exists.
